deep.reconstruction:
Problem: build a 'dictionary' between morphisms of topoi and recollement (Artin gluing) data. The aim, continued on the next page, is to define relative cohomology of a morphism of topoi (the cohomology of its 'mapping cone') and its long exact sequence. This sits inside a folder on asphericity: the previous page treats i_!, i^*, i_* for A_0 -> A and 0-aspheric inclusions.

Step 1. Take a morphism of topoi f: X_0 -> X_1. View it as a fibred topos over Δ_1 = {0 -> 1}, with fibres X_0 and X_1. Its total topos is X = C(f), which Grothendieck calls the 'mapping-cone'. Its sheaves are triples (F_0, F_1, u), with F_i a sheaf on X_i and u: f^*F_1 -> F_0, or equivalently the adjoint map F_1 -> f_*F_0.

Step 2. This is exactly the Artin gluing of SGA4 IV 9.5:
- X_0 is an open subtopos of X;
- X_1 is the complementary closed subtopos;
- the gluing functor φ: F(X_0) -> F(X_1) (left exact in the general theory) is φ = f_*.

Step 3. Claim: the closed inclusion i_1: X_1 -> X is 'strictly cohomologically trivial', i.e. H^*(X, F) ≅ H^*(X_1, F_1) for every F = (F_0, F_1, u). Proof sketch, using the marginal 'Re NB':
- There is a retraction r: X -> X_1 with r^*(G) = (f^*G, G, id).
- A morphism (f^*G, G, id) -> (F_0, F_1, u) is the same as a map G -> F_1. So r^* is left adjoint to i_1^*, i.e. i_1^* = r_*.
- In degree 0, a global section of X is a pair (a_0, a_1) with a_0 = u∘f^*a_1. It is therefore determined by a_1, so Γ(X, F) = Γ(X_1, F_1).
- i_1^* is exact. It has an exact left adjoint r^*, so it preserves injectives.
- Hence the derived functors agree: H^*(X, -) = H^*(X_1, i_1^* -).
Topologically, the mapping cylinder deformation-retracts onto the target.

Step 4 (margins).
- X lies over Top(Δ_1), the Sierpiński topos, with X_0 the preimage of the open point.
- X = (X_0 × Δ_1) ⊔_{X_0×{1}} X_1, the mapping-cylinder pushout.

Next page. Recollement data (U, Z, φ) come from a morphism of topoi exactly when φ preserves all limits and its left adjoint is left exact. Relative cohomology H^i_{X_1}(X, F) =: H^i(X_1 mod X_0, F) then fits into the exact sequence ... -> H^i_{X_1}(X, F) -> H^i(X_1, F_1) -> H^i(X_0, F_0) -> H^{i+1}_{X_1}(X, F) -> ...
errors: Terminology: the gluing topos C(f) is the mapping CYLINDER of f, not the mapping cone. Grothendieck's own marginal pushout formula (X_0×Δ_1) ⊔ X_1 is the cylinder. The cone appears only implicitly, via cohomology of the pair (X, X_0), i.e. 'X_1 mod X_0' on the next page.
Notational slips: the target is written 𝒴_1 in (1) but 𝒳_1 afterwards. The map is written f_0^* where f^* is meant.

The cohomological claim (3) is stated without proof; it is correct. It holds because i_1^* = r_* has the exact left adjoint r^* (the retraction in the margin), so i_1^* is exact and preserves injectives. The argument is for abelian sheaves; for nonabelian H^1 the analogous statement also holds via the same retraction.

ideas.what: A morphism of topoi viewed as a fibred topos over Δ_1, with total topos given by Artin gluing along φ = f_* (sheaves = triples (F_0, F_1, f^*F_1 -> F_0))
ideas.modern_name: Artin gluing Gl(f_*) / topos-theoretic mapping cylinder / cocomma object with the Sierpiński topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: Artin and Grothendieck (SGA4 IV 9.5), Wraith (Artin glueing, 1974), Johnstone (Topos Theory 1977; Elephant)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exp. IV §9.5 (recollement); fibred topoi over categories in SGA4 VI

ideas.what: Mapping cylinder as a pushout (X_0 × Top(Δ_1)) ⊔_{X_0×{1}} X_1, with a structural map X -> Top(Δ_1)
ideas.modern_name: Mapping cylinder of topoi via the Sierpiński topos (lax colimit / cocomma)

ideas.what: Closed inclusion of the target into the cylinder is cohomologically trivial (deformation retraction r with r^* ⊣ i_1^*, i.e. i_1 essential with left-exact i_{1!})
ideas.modern_name: Mapping cylinder retracts onto target; aspheric closed embedding

ideas.what: Characterization of recollements coming from geometric morphisms (φ continuous with left-exact left adjoint), and relative cohomology of a morphism of topoi as local cohomology on the cylinder (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Relative cohomology of a morphism of topoi / cohomology of the mapping cone
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; cf. Johnstone on gluing; Deligne-style mapping cones of simplicial objects

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a clean, correct dictionary between morphisms of topoi and Artin gluing (φ = f_*), with the mapping-cylinder retraction and cohomological triviality of the target. All of this is standard in SGA4 IV 9.5 and Johnstone/Wraith. The only mild interest is its placement in an early-1980s asphericity/homotopy-of-topoi programme, a precursor to Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs, and the calling of the cylinder a 'mapping-cone'.
transcription_corrections: '(exact ig.)' should read '(exact à g.)', i.e. left exact, referring to the gluing functor of the general theory.
'u : f_0^*(F_1)' is in substance u : f^*(F_1) -> F_0.
In (1), the target '𝒴_1' is the same object as 𝒳_1 used throughout.
The left marginal near (1) reads roughly 'Dictionnaire morphismes de topos / changements [?] de topos'; it is uncertain.
After 'est strictement' there is a crossed-out word with an interlinear insertion; the intended meaning is 'cohomologiquement trivial' / aspheric, consistent with 'strict asphérique' on page 4.
